lacuna.name: cuda-graph-atomic-reduction
lacuna.repo_anchor: MEMORY.md 2026-08-28 entries (split-K graph capture): 'the atomicAdd accumulation pattern requires WS to be zeroed between replays, which the current graph capture does not express... Fix options: dedicated memset node in the graph, or per-split output buffers with a final reduction'; software/vllm/sm75-marlin/turing_lab/probes/cuda_graph_validation.md 'Split-K flow: WS-zero replay ordering (OPEN)' records the deterministic wrong value 16.47 persisting across replays and fix options (1) store-only for num_splits=1, (2) per-split buffers + final reduction, (3) in-kernel cudaMemsetAsync prologue; plan/0002-turing-marlin-backend/runtime-validation.md records the dense kernel graph-safe PASS with this split-K item as the remaining runtime lane blocker; plan/0002-turing-marlin-backend/marlin-contract.md lines 120-131 and 144-150 document the incumbent's caller-zeroed workspace ('workspace (zeroed by the caller, marlin_make_workspace_new) backs the global reduction locks') and the no-host-sync requirement that makes capture legal.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the ecosystem has converged on three reusable fix patterns, and two of them already exist in this fork's own tree. (1) In-graph zeroing nodes: recording a memset/fill before the split launch works semantically (stream capture turns cudaMemsetAsync into a memset node), but the PyTorch forums thread 'Slowdown in CUDA graph execution using cudaMemsetAsync (vs. a fill kernel)' (Oct 3-14 2024, flagged for NVIDIA awareness, unresolved) measured on H100-SXM5 that a 4-byte memset node itself runs ~800ns-1.7us yet introduces ~10-13us gaps between kernels during replay; a 1000-op graph microbenchmark showed memset nodes 34.8ms vs fill-kernel (tensor.zero_()) 33.4ms (~5% end-to-end); in eager mode memset is actually faster (~0.8us vs 1.1-1.3us), so the penalty is graph-replay-specific; workaround is to prefer fill kernels, and library-internal memsets (cuBLAS, TransformerEngine) are not workaroundable. (2) In-kernel self-cleaning synchronization, already shipped in the incumbent Marlin template the fork carries (software/vllm/sm75-marlin/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/marlin_template.h): the non-atomic path uses a turnstile - barrier_acquire(&locks[locks_off], slice_idx) spins until the lock reaches the slice index so slices reduce in fixed order, and barrier_release(lock, reset=last) writes the lock back to 0, leaving the workspace zeroed for the next launch/replay; the use_atomic_add path (lines ~457-473, ~176-223, ~2001-2023) has slice 0 zero the destination buffer in-kernel and then set locks[locks_off] = 1 - slice_count (negative); every other slice does wait_negative_and_add (spin on ld.global.acquire until negative, then atomicAdd 1 after its own atomicAdd into C), so the lock returns to exactly 0 when all slices finish - replay-safe with zero external memset. (3) Deterministic restructure: per-split output buffers plus a fixed-order final reduction kernel - the Stream-K paper (arXiv 2301.03598, Osama et al., Jan 2023, PPoPP'23 poster; 55+ citations) describes outputting each split part separately and reducing deterministically in a subsequent kernel; CUTLASS 3.x sm90 stream-K implements the barrier ('turnstile') fixup workspace (sm90_tile_scheduler_stream_k.hpp) with a Deterministic mode (CTAs reduce sequentially in K order) and a Nondeterministic mode (atomic reduce into workspace, order varies; subject of logic bug NVIDIA/cutlass issue #2027); CUTLASS 2.x pre-Hopper split-K exposes Serial and Parallel (per-part buffers + separate reduction kernel) reduction policies. Thinking Machines Lab, 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' (Horace He, Sep 10 2025), frames the industry position: atomics are usually absent from a forward pass and are not the typical nondeterminism source; the real target is batch invariance, achieved by compiling one kernel config for all shapes (avoiding split-K and tile-size switches; ~20% matmul cost with an unoptimized Triton kernel; end-to-end vLLM Qwen-3-8B 55s deterministic vs 26s default, 42s with a better attention kernel); it cites split/tree reductions, a serial cleanup reduction, or semaphores enforcing a fixed accumulation order (CUTLASS-style) as deterministic atomic replacements, notes NVLink-SHARP in-switch reductions are deterministic on Blackwell and Hopper with CUDA 12.8+, and does not discuss CUDA graphs. NVIDIA CCCL (developer blog 'Controlling Floating-Point Determinism in NVIDIA CCCL', Mar 5 2026; CCCL 3.1) codifies reduction determinism levels: not_guaranteed (atomics enabled, fastest), run_to_run (default; fixed tree of intra-thread/warp/block reductions plus a second aggregation kernel, no atomics), gpu_to_gpu (reproducible floating-point accumulator with exponent binning) - confirming the framing that atomic order is the nondeterminism source and fixed-order trees are the deterministic substitute. Hardware-theory anchor: DAB 'Deterministic Atomic Buffering' (Chou, Ng, Cattell, Intan, Sinclair, Devietti, Aamodt; MICRO-53, Oct 2020; IEEE 9251962) proves atomics can be made deterministic via hardware per-address buffering with low overhead, but it is an architectural proposal, not deployable on existing GPUs. Nearby vLLM evidence of the bug class: issue #11205 'Corrupted output with GPTQ Marlin kernel' (opened Dec 14 2024, closed by PR #11493) - corrupted values at varying indices per invocation, traced via compute-sanitizer to three cp_async pipeline races in gptq_marlin.cu/marlin.cuh (separate defect, same sanitiser-based workflow). No public documentation found of TensorRT-LLM's internal split-K workspace zeroing under captured graphs [uncertain].
lacuna.sm75_viability: Everything needed for all three fix patterns runs on TU102 today, and two are already proven on this exact host. Measured on this rig (2x Quadro RTX 6000, clocks locked 1455 MHz, CUDA 13.3.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130): the incumbent Marlin kernel - which uses exactly the turnstile-lock global reduce and (when enabled) the atomicAdd negative-lock handshake - achieves 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 across the model shapes, so the barrier/lock primitives (ld.global.acquire.gpu.b32, fence.acq_rel.gpu, red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.s32, atomicAdd on fp16x2 pairs via c_scalar_t2) are all sm_75-functional; the fork's dense w4a16_opt2 kernel is graph-safe (capture, replay, post-replay mutation recomputed, PASS); the fork's split-K eager path is oracle-validated (float64 oracle ALL PASS at N256/K512/G64, 2.52 TFLOP/s at M16/N4096/K4096) and the graph-replayed split-K deterministically returns the wrong value 16.47 because the WS.zero_ fill's ordering versus the atomicAdd accumulations is not expressed by the capture. No capability floor is involved: no TMA, clusters, or sm_80 mma are needed - the CUTLASS 3.x sm90 stream-K scheduler itself (TMA/cluster-based) is NOT portable to sm_75, but only its turnstile-barrier idea is needed, and the incumbent marlin_template.h already demonstrates the port on Turing. CUTLASS 2.x ships sm_75 split-K GEMMs with Serial and Parallel reduction policies as reference implementations of the deterministic option. The memset-node alternative is viable but carries the measured replay-gap penalty (~10-13us per memset node on H100; the TU102-specific magnitude is unmeasured [uncertain]) - on a decode graph with one memset per layer this could cost tens of microseconds per replay, material relative to small-M GEMM times. The attention-backend matrix and Triton mma.884/FMA codegen gates do not apply to this item; the only gating mechanism is the CUDA-graph memory-dependency semantics, which are architecture-independent.
lacuna.upstream_base: Fork tracks vLLM main of the V1-engine era: source build against CUDA 13.3.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, driver 610.57.04, environment aligned 2026-08-27 (plan/0002-turing-marlin-backend/environment.md); branch sm75-marlin pinned tip 711b6898c4, last fork change to marlin_template.h at 7021be66 Jun 12 2026. Ledger lines: (a) the lock-based global-reduce turnstile has been in Marlin since the IST-DASLab import into vLLM (early 2024) and is unchanged in shape (barrier_acquire/barrier_release with reset-to-zero) through current main; (b) the use_atomic_add slice-0 in-kernel zeroing plus locks = 1 - slice_count negative handshake is present in current upstream marlin_template.h (exact introducing vLLM release not pinned [uncertain]); (c) vLLM issue #11205 (Dec 2024) fixed by PR #11493 (early 2025 [uncertain exact merge date]) for the cp_async race class; (d) CUTLASS: stream-K in 3.x from 2023 (arXiv 2301.03598), sm90_tile_scheduler_stream_k.hpp deterministic/nondeterministic modes on main, issue #2027 open on the nondeterministic-mode logic; (e) CCCL determinism API in CCCL 3.1 (blog Mar 5 2026); (f) no upstream vLLM release dropped or degraded sm_75 for this surface - the incumbent kernels compile and run on TU102 in the fork today.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Small, kernel-ladder-scale item, not a campaign: land one fix pattern in the turing_lab split-K kernel and re-run the existing graph validation probe. (a) Port the incumbent's slice-0 in-kernel zero + negative-lock handshake: ~40-60 lines, ~1 day, smallest diff; (b) port the turnstile barrier_acquire/barrier_release(reset) global reduce: ~1-2 days including the fp32 workspace reduce; (c) per-split output buffers + final reduction kernel (deterministic): ~2-3 days including workspace sizing and the reduction kernel. Each variant plus graph re-capture, 100-replay oracle re-check, and a result note in cuda_graph_validation.md; budget 2-4 sessions total including the A/B timing of memset node vs fill node vs in-kernel zero on TU102.
effort_value.unlocks: Unblocks the graph-captured decode step for the optimized Turing backend (the runtime lane's remaining item): split-K is the designated small-M strategy where the pipelined kernel currently leads (0.24/1.85/6.72 TFLOP/s at M 1/2/4 vs the incumbent's sweep-leading small-M numbers), so a graph-safe split-K is what lets decode batches use the new kernel end-to-end; unlocks the MoE dispatch path (same capture requirements); closes the last runtime blocker before the D8 report; and directly serves the operator's serving target of graph-captured decode on TU102.
effort_value.dependency_order: Internal: depends only on the split-K kernel itself (already landed and float64-oracle-validated eager) and on the existing CUDA-graph probe harness (cuda_graph_validation.md flow); the dense kernel's graph-safety is already proven and independent. Can proceed in parallel with: the repack-interleave/register-dequant performance work, the rope sm_86 reference run (needs the llama-server window), and D8 report drafting. Is a prerequisite for: the full-decode CUDA-graph campaign and the MoE runtime path. External prerequisites: none - every primitive (global acquire loads, relaxed atomic adds, in-kernel zeroing) is already exercised in-tree by the incumbent kernel on this hardware.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) atomicAdd ordering makes the memset/fill-node and in-kernel-handshake variants run-to-run nondeterministic in fp32 accumulation order - correct per replay (starts from zero) but not bitwise reproducible; only the turnstile or per-split-buffer variants are order-fixed. (2) The memset-node option carries the measured replay-gap penalty (~10-13us per node on H100, PyTorch forums Oct 2024) and can silently regress decode latency while fixing numerics. (3) Turnstile spin-waits (ld.global.acquire loops) deadlock if a waiting slice's predecessor is never scheduled - the incumbent avoids this via its persistent-kernel stripe scheduling; the port must copy the scheduling invariant, not just the barrier code. (4) Silent-fallback risk: for num_splits==1 the atomic path must degenerate to a plain store (cuda_graph_validation.md option 1) - keep that branch explicit. (5) The failure mode of this bug class is deterministic-but-wrong (16.47), which the float64 oracle catches only if the oracle is run against graph-replay output, not eager output. Upstream drift: vLLM's marlin_template.h is actively churned (fp8, awq, MoE variants, bias), so a port diff conflicts on rebase; the fork is pinned, making the exposure bounded to the next deliberate rebase.
effort_value.determinism_class: By fix choice the mechanism lands in one of two classes. Class A (replay-correct, order-nondeterministic): memset/fill-node zeroing + atomicAdd, or the incumbent's in-kernel slice-0 zero + negative-lock handshake - each replay starts from a zeroed destination so results are correct, but the atomic accumulation order varies replay-to-replay, giving statistical (non-bitwise) reproducibility; run-to-run variance source is atomic scheduling order only (graph structure itself replays deterministically). Class B (bitwise run-to-run deterministic): the turnstile (slices reduce in slice-index order under barrier_acquire) or per-split output buffers + fixed-order final reduction - identical inputs give identical bits on every replay, matching the Marlin default path and CUTLASS stream-K Deterministic mode; this is also what CCCL labels run_to_run determinism (fixed reduction tree, no atomics) versus not_guaranteed (atomics). The house discipline holds if: the float64-oracle gate is run against graph-replay outputs (catches the 16.47 deterministic-wrong class), and median-of-N over >=100 replays is used for any timing so Class A's order variance washes out of perf numbers while Class B permits exact-diff regression tests. Restart-to-restart: graph topology is fixed at capture, so the only in-graph nondeterminism is atomic order; eager-vs-graph must still be oracle-compared separately since capture reorders the zero-fill dependency. gpu_to_gpu (cross-device bitwise, CCCL's RFA-style binned accumulation) is out of scope for a single TU102 host.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: it is the last open runtime-lane item before the D8 report and the direct gate on graph-captured decode - the operator's stated serving target; the fix patterns are proven in-tree (the incumbent Marlin kernel solved this exact problem on this exact TU102 hardware with the turnstile and negative-lock handshake, so the port is low-risk copying, not research); effort is days, not weeks; and the bug is of the deterministic-wrong class the house oracle discipline exists to catch. Against: option 1 (store-only for num_splits==1) already gives a graph-correct fallback if the serving path only ever uses single-split under the graph, and the small-M win could alternatively come from deeper pipelining - so if the D8 deadline dominates, a scoped num_splits==1 store-only fix plus a documented limitation is a defensible cheaper close. Window-closing risk is low: this is fork-internal engineering paced by the host, not ecosystem-paced.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 probe (oracle first, no timing until numerics pass): on the existing split-K oracle case (N256/K512/G64 plus the M16/N4096/K4096 shape), capture the graph under each candidate fix - (a) fill-kernel node (WS.zero_-style torch op) recorded before the split launch, (b) cudaMemsetAsync memset node, (c) ported slice-0 in-kernel zero + negative lock, (d) turnstile barrier reduce - then replay 100 times; after each replay, copy out the result and diff against the float64 oracle under fp16 tolerance, and separately read back the WS/lock bytes between replays asserting they are zero (the self-cleaning invariant). Any deterministic wrong value (the 16.47 signature) fails the variant. Only after all replays pass: time replays on locked clocks (1455 MHz) to quantify the memset-node gap penalty on TU102 versus the fill node and the in-kernel variants, and record the A/B table in cuda_graph_validation.md.
